FIX ROUND 744d for story #744 (tui: the fleet refresh re-folds every event of every run every 2 s, so on a 745k-event journal it never stops folding and keys lag by seconds), on branch story-744-fleet-refresh, already checked out in this worktree at 82dca088.

You are fixing exactly the finding below and nothing beside it. Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED. Build to it.

OPERATOR RULINGS:
- The operator reported #744 on 2026-10-18 ("with my current brokkr db, when I open the TUI and want to navigate, things are extremely slow").
- Decision 0014: readouts are read-only.
- Decision 0001: the journal is the hash-chained source of truth, and a readout must not show a run healthy that a whole read refuses.
- 2026-09-26, the threat model: catch realistic ACCIDENTAL misuse, and fail closed on what cannot be read. A deliberate, exotic evasion is a LOW residual.
- The schema of `events` is NOT changed in this story, and no table, index or meta row is added. The operator has a separate proposed decision (#753, 0089) on a derived read model; do not anticipate it here.

HISTORY OF THE BRANCH (cut from main 8bd34fdb; your diff is judged against 82dca088)
- 50488082: the kept fleet, the off-loop reader, `brokkr runs` on the kept read. Decision 0088 is proposed.
- f5a0800a answered the first review's seven findings.
- b5790ad6 (744b): the kept fleet bound to the journal file; a frame draws none of a run or seat the shell has left while its read is out (CONFIRMED).
- 82dca088 (744c): each kept run's rows at or below its head are counted (Store::rows_through, KeptFleet's recount), and a run whose count is not its head's seq is read whole. The read is bound to the file only when the file is stated alike before the store opens and after the read. The equal-length copy-over quarantines with the exact text (CONFIRMED by all three positions). BUT the count runs only when the main journal file's (length, mtime, ctime) moved since the last refresh (Journal::unwritten), and the review held that gate: see below.
- When you are done, the branch is the above plus ONE new commit of yours. Do not rebase, squash, amend or merge main.

FIX THIS (the review chief over 82dca088, quoted):

1. HIGH, security (decisions 0001, 0088 ruling 2, 0071 ruling 9). "The written-since gate (fleet/kept.rs Journal::unwritten, read in KeptFleet::refresh) stats only the main journal file, but the store runs in WAL mode (brokkr-store schema::ensure_wal): every committed transaction lands in <db>-wal and the main file is written only at a checkpoint. So a same-head damaged copy restored through SQLite's backup API (sqlite3 .restore, Python backup) or any prefix change committed into the WAL, while a connection keeps the WAL un-checkpointed (held open, or under the 1000-page auto-checkpoint), leaves device, inode, length, mtime AND ctime of the main file identical; recount is skipped, load_after confirms only the head row, the run is carried Folded. ... after PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) the next refresh drew 'journal chain: event 2: seq is not contiguous (expected 1)'. This is the store's own write path, not an exotic evasion ... 0088 ruling 2's words 'which any write moves' are false of the main file under WAL."
   THE CONTROLLER'S CALL (the chief left it to the controller): run the count on EVERY refresh, UNGATED. Delete the written-since gate (Journal::unwritten and the (length, mtime, ctime) fields it alone reads). Do not replace it with a stat of the -wal sidecar or any other file clock: a gate on file clocks has now been held twice, and the coarse-clock LOW (finding 3 below) goes with it. Keep the (device, inode) identity that drops the whole kept fleet, and keep 744c's two-sided statement.
   - Measure on the operator-shaped generated journal (1,164 runs, ~745k events, 95% checkpoints; the branch's existing generator): state the idle refresh's time and peak, warm, in the commit message and in decision 0088. The chief measured the count at 18 ms warm, and the idle refresh at about 33 ms with it. That is accepted. If your measurement exceeds 50 ms for the idle refresh, say so in notes with the numbers, and do not gate the count to hide it.
   - Regression, in kept_tests AND tui_read's read tests: hold a read-write connection open on the journal, commit a prefix loss for a kept run into the WAL (rusqlite's `backup` feature may be enabled for tests only, as a dev-dependency feature; or, on the held connection, drop the append-only trigger and DELETE seq 1), and assert that the main file's (length, mtime, ctime) are unchanged and a -wal file is present. The next refresh reads the run whole and shows the whole read's quarantine with exact text. Removal control: gate the count on the main file's (length, mtime, ctime) again and see the regression fail with its stated text. Record it in the commit message.
   - The existing tests (the equal-length copy-over, Moved, Shorter, the different-head test, the VACUUMed test, rows_through's store test, the two-sided statement) still pass, with exact values unchanged except where the removed gate made a value.
   - The idle work-count observable: an idle refresh on an unmoved journal still reads 0 events. The count reads index entries, not events; say so.

DECISION 0088: make ruling 2 true of what you build. The count runs on every refresh, so a lost or added row at or below a kept head is seen at the next refresh, through any write path, WAL included. Remove "which any write moves" and every other sentence the deleted gate made true. Keep the disclosed residual in ruling 2 for the operator, worded to match (finding 2 below). Change no other words unless one is false.

CARRY, do not change (each goes in your notes for the PR):
2. LOW (disclosed in 0088 ruling 2; the operator rules on it): a row below a kept head whose CONTENT changed in place at the same count and head. That needs a writer that defeats the append-only triggers, or corruption SQLite reads cleanly. Inspect, export, brokkr runs, a console's first refresh and a run entered verify it whole; an open console keeps the fold until the head moves; `r` reads the open run whole, not the fleet.
3. LOW (the coarse file clock): it goes with the gate. Say in notes that it is closed by the deletion.
4. INFO: quality/public-api/brokkr-store.txt grows by Store::rows_through. The PR names it on its Ruling: line.
- 744b's frame fix (terminal::held_to, terminal::unread, reader.rs Asked::frames) stays untouched. Kept::read's only reader is the acceptance work-count test. Keep every function you touch at CC 15 or under (refresh 8, recount 3, rows_through 2, run_of 6, read_views 14 today). Decision 0088 ruling 5 (checkpoint bodies still parsed for chain verification) stays the operator's ruling to make.

For the implement phase: fix, then run, all clean, from the worktree root: cargo fmt --all -- --check; cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -- -D warnings; cargo test -p brokkr-store --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-view --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib --locked; cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it --locked (timeout 590; split by FILE:: filters if longer, and name each); typos --hidden; quality/ratchet.sh files, clones and api; `cargo crap --path <crate>/src --format json` for every function you add or change; git diff --check.

Every review position, panel member or chief, is READ-ONLY: it changes no tracked file and makes no commit, whatever this text asks. It reports each finding. Only the implement phase fixes a finding the review returns. Reviewers: reproduce the WAL-held prefix loss against HEAD's binary (a console open in a PTY, the loss committed into a held connection's WAL, no checkpoint) and see the next refresh quarantine the run. Then judge whether the residual 0088 ruling 2 names is the only one left, naming any other write path you can reach.

Commit one signed-off commit (git commit -s), message "tui: <what changed> (#744)" in the repository's style, ending with the line "Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>". Never push. Run every command in the foreground and wait for it: never background a command or schedule a wakeup, because a headless seat ends when it waits. Do not run scripts/coverage-exact.sh; the controller runs it.

HOST FACTS AND PARALLEL WORK

Stay out of it: decision 0065 slice two (the-forge-b9; NEVER message it, or any brokkr-wt-* seat) holds brokkr-runtime engine/broker*, engine.rs, brokkr-protocol hands*. #288 slices L and M edit brokkr-runtime agents/ and bundle/compose.rs. #349 slice 8 edits brokkr-runtime dispatch sites. #753 is docs only (decision 0089). #735 edits brokkr-cli recipes/agents.rs. This round touches only brokkr-cli fleet/, tui_read.rs, their tests, brokkr-store read.rs and its tests if needed, Cargo.toml dev-dependency features if needed, and decision 0088.

# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.
